labs.name: Glucose
labs.notes: Fasting reference range. Postprandial values up to 140 mg/dL considered normal.

labs.name: Hemoglobin A1c
labs.notes: 5.7-6.4% = prediabetes; >=6.5% = diabetes. ADA target for most adults with diabetes: <7.0%.

labs.name: Creatinine
labs.notes: Male range 0.7-1.3; Female range 0.6-1.1. Must be interpreted with eGFR.

labs.name: Blood Urea Nitrogen (BUN)
labs.notes: BUN/Creatinine ratio >20:1 suggests prerenal azotemia.

labs.name: eGFR (CKD-EPI)
labs.notes: >=90 normal, 60-89 mild decrease, 45-59 mild-moderate, 30-44 moderate-severe, 15-29 severe, <15 kidney failure.

labs.name: Sodium
labs.notes: Hyponatremia <136; Hypernatremia >145. Critical values require immediate intervention.

labs.name: Potassium
labs.notes: Critical values carry risk of cardiac arrhythmia. Check for hemolysis if unexpectedly elevated.

labs.name: Chloride
labs.notes: Interpret with sodium and bicarbonate for acid-base assessment.

labs.name: Bicarbonate (CO2)
labs.notes: Low values suggest metabolic acidosis; high values suggest metabolic alkalosis.

labs.name: Calcium
labs.notes: Correct for albumin: Corrected Ca = measured Ca + 0.8 * (4.0 - albumin).

labs.name: Magnesium
labs.notes: Hypomagnesemia can cause refractory hypokalemia and hypocalcemia.

labs.name: Phosphorus
labs.notes: Elevated in CKD. Low in refeeding syndrome and DKA treatment.

labs.name: Hemoglobin
labs.notes: Male 13.5-17.5; Female 12.0-16.0. Transfusion threshold typically <7 g/dL (restrictive).

labs.name: White Blood Cell Count (WBC)
labs.notes: Leukocytosis >11; Leukopenia <4.5. Neutropenia (ANC <1500) is clinically significant.

labs.name: Platelet Count
labs.notes: Thrombocytopenia <150; Thrombocytosis >400. Spontaneous bleeding risk increases <20.

labs.name: Mean Corpuscular Volume (MCV)
labs.notes: Microcytic <80 (iron deficiency, thalassemia); Macrocytic >100 (B12/folate deficiency, MDS).

labs.name: ALT (Alanine Aminotransferase)
labs.notes: More specific for liver injury than AST. >3x ULN considered significant elevation.

labs.name: AST (Aspartate Aminotransferase)
labs.notes: Also elevated in cardiac and skeletal muscle injury. AST/ALT ratio >2 suggests alcoholic liver disease.

labs.name: Alkaline Phosphatase (ALP)
labs.notes: Elevated in cholestasis, bone disease, pregnancy. GGT helps distinguish hepatic from bone source.

labs.name: Total Bilirubin
labs.notes: Direct (conjugated) >0.3 suggests hepatocellular or obstructive disease. Indirect elevation in hemolysis or Gilbert syndrome.

labs.name: Albumin
labs.notes: Low in liver disease, nephrotic syndrome, malnutrition, inflammation. Half-life ~20 days.

labs.name: Total Cholesterol
labs.notes: Desirable <200; Borderline high 200-239; High >=240.

labs.name: Triglycerides
labs.notes: Normal <150; Borderline 150-199; High 200-499; Very high >=500 (pancreatitis risk).

labs.name: HDL Cholesterol
labs.notes: Low HDL (<40 men, <50 women) is an independent cardiovascular risk factor.

labs.name: LDL Cholesterol (calculated)
labs.notes: Optimal <100; Near optimal 100-129; Borderline 130-159; High 160-189; Very high >=190. ASCVD target varies by risk.

labs.name: Carbon Dioxide (CO2) Partial Pressure
labs.notes: Arterial blood gas. Low = respiratory alkalosis or compensation for metabolic acidosis.

labs.name: Oxygen Partial Pressure (PaO2)
labs.notes: Hypoxemia <80 mmHg. Severe hypoxemia <60 mmHg. Age-adjusted: expected PaO2 = 104 - (0.27 * age).

labs.name: Arterial pH
labs.notes: Acidemia <7.35; Alkalemia >7.45. Incompatible with life below ~6.8 or above ~7.8.

labs.name: Prothrombin Time (PT)
labs.notes: Prolonged in warfarin therapy, liver disease, DIC, vitamin K deficiency.

labs.name: INR (International Normalized Ratio)
labs.notes: Therapeutic range for warfarin: 2.0-3.0 (most indications) or 2.5-3.5 (mechanical valve).

labs.name: TSH (Thyroid Stimulating Hormone)
labs.notes: Low TSH = hyperthyroidism (or over-replacement); High TSH = hypothyroidism. Interpret with free T4.

labs.name: Free T4 (Thyroxine)
labs.notes: Interpret with TSH. Low free T4 + high TSH = primary hypothyroidism.

labs.name: Troponin I
labs.notes: Elevation indicates myocardial injury. Serial measurements needed (0h, 3h, 6h). High-sensitivity assays have lower thresholds.

labs.name: BNP (B-type Natriuretic Peptide)
labs.notes: <100 = HF unlikely; 100-400 = possible HF (correlate clinically); >400 = HF likely. Age and renal function affect levels.

labs.name: NT-proBNP
labs.notes: Age-stratified: <50y: <450; 50-75y: <900; >75y: <1800 to rule out acute HF. Renal clearance dependent.

labs.name: Glucose (fasting)
labs.notes: 100-125 = impaired fasting glucose (prediabetes); >=126 = diabetes (requires confirmation).

labs.name: Microalbumin/Creatinine Ratio (UACR)
labs.notes: 30-300 = moderately increased albuminuria (microalbuminuria); >300 = severely increased (macroalbuminuria). Screen annually in diabetes.

labs.name: Uric Acid
labs.notes: Male 3.4-7.0; Female 2.4-6.0. Elevated in gout, tumor lysis syndrome, CKD.

labs.name: LDH (Lactate Dehydrogenase)
labs.notes: Nonspecific marker elevated in hemolysis, tissue injury, malignancy, liver disease.

labs.name: Hemoglobin A1c (IFCC standardized)
labs.notes: IFCC units. 39-47 = prediabetes; >=48 = diabetes. ADA target for most adults: <53 mmol/mol.
